 Series History: ECU, Memphis no stranger to dramatic finishes
 The last three meetings between the Pirates and Tigers came down to the final play. 
 Stephen Igoe 1 
 If you're looking for heart-stopping endings, there's a high probability a matchup between East Carolina and Memphis on the football field - at least based on recent history - will deliver. 
 The last three meetings between the two sides have been decided by a combined seven points. ECU, luckily from its point of view, has been been on the victorious side on all those occasions. And dating back to when the series first started in 1990, the Pirates have won 18 meetings compared to the Tigers eight wins. 
 Thursday night's kickoff will represent the 27th all-time meeting between the Pirates and Tigers in football. The start time inside Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium in Tennessee is set for 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 CT) on ESPN2.
 Last year's game, on Nov. 15, 2025, was a back and forth affair in front of 37,438 that was ultimately decided on Katin Houser's 31-yard touchdown pass to Payton Mangrum with 1:08 left in the game. ECU wound up victorious, 31-27. The Pirates ended up completing the season 9-4 overall. Memphis, in the last year of the Ryan Silverfield era, went 8-5. 
 It was also a classic during the 2022 season, which was also played in Greenville. Quarterbacks Seth Henigan (407 passing yards) and Holton Ahlers (304 passing yards) combined to throw for 711 yards, but Henigan's final pass in the fourth overtime fell incomplete, giving ECU a 47-45 win in probably the craziest game of the series. Memphis led the game 17-0 in the second quarter before ECU roared back to tie it, and ultimately take a 30-23 lead late in the fourth quarter. Memphis mounted a game-tying drive and score, with 19 seconds left. That forced overtime, where the teams traded blows before ECU ultimately prevailed.
 The last time the two sides met in Memphis was 2021. That was also an overtime game that was won by ECU, 30-29. Both teams scored a touchdown in OT, before Memphis opted to go for two and the win. But Henigan's pass was broken up. ECU ended up securing the win, and getting bowl eligibility for the first time since the 2016 campaign. East Carolina finished that game a remarkable 18-for-26 on third down and with 502 yards of offense.
 The two prior times ECU and Memphis met, during the Scottie Montgomery era, were much more forgettable for Pirate fans. Memphis hung 70 on ECU in a 70-13 win in 2017, and defeated ECU in Greenville, 59-41, in 2018.
 East Carolina won seven in a row from 2006-12, when both teams were in Conference USA. The Pirates also had a five-game winning streak from 1994-1998. Memphis' longest winning streak in the series was three games, from 2003-05.
 Memphis hit a game-winning field goal with six seconds left in 2004, as Stephen Gostowski converted a 35-yarder inside Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium. That contest featured 225 rushing yards and four touchdowns by Memphis running back Deangelo Williams, as well as 43 rushing yards and a score by ECU running back Chris Johnson. Both went on to be NFL All-Pros.
 Nine of the 26 games in the series have been decided by one possession. ECU is 8-5 all-time at Memphis.
